        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R28 +3V3 SCL0_GPIO45 10"}

      "impact": "The SCL0 line cannot be driven low within I2C timing limits, and the bus would be heavily loaded. Communication on the J5 I2C header would fail or be unreliable.",
      "confidence": 0.7
    },
    {
      "category": "wrong_value",
      "components": ["R16", "R17"],
      "pins": ["R16.1", "R16.2", "R17.1", "R17.2", "U12.3"],

      "expected": "A 12 V output from a 0.2 V feedback reference needs a bottom resistor of about 30 kΩ for a 1.8 MΩ top resistor (ratio ≈ 59).",
      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "R16 | 205k | Resistor_SMD:R_0603_1608Metric | Device:R"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "R17 | 1.8M | Resistor_SMD:R_0603_1608Metric | Device:R"},

        {"source": "spice", "quote": "R16 0 FB 205k"}
      ],
      "impact": "The +12V boost rail would regulate near 2 V instead of 12 V, which would starve or fail any 12 V load on that rail.",
      "confidence": 0.3
    },
    {

      "components": ["Q1", "U6"],
      "pins": ["Q1.2", "Q1.3", "U6.1", "U6.6"],
      "nets": ["+5V", "USBC_VBUS_IN", "Net-(Q1-G)"],
      "observed": "In the LTC4412 ideal-diode stage, the PMOS Q1 has its source (Q1.2) on +5V, which is the LTC4412 SENSE node (U6.6), and its drain (Q1.3) on USBC_VBUS_IN, which is the LTC4412 VIN node (U6.1). The device's input-side source arrangement appears reversed relative to a standard VIN-to-load ideal diode.",
      "expected": "For reverse-current blocking, the PMOS source should sit on the VIN (USB VBUS) side and its drain on the load side (+5V), so the body diode is oriented to block reverse flow.",

        {"source": "spec", "quote": "USB input \"OR-ing\"/protection circuitry (LTC4412 ideal-diode controller, U6)"}
      ],
      "impact": "Reverse-current protection could be defeated through the PMOS body diode, and the USB/+5V power-path behaviour may not match the intended ideal-diode function.",
      "confidence": 0.25
    }

}

anomalies.observed: R28 is valued "10" (10 ohm) and pulls the SCL0_GPIO45 I2C line (J5.2 / Module1.80 SCL0) up to +3V3. Its partner pull-up R23 on SDA0_GPIO44 is 10k, so the two lines of the same I2C bus have pull-ups differing by three orders of magnitude.
anomalies.expected: I2C pull-ups should be in the kilohm range, matching the 10k pull-up on the paired SDA0 line (R23). A 10 ohm pull-up would draw about 330 mA when the line is pulled low, far beyond what the CM4 GPIO can sink.
anomalies.impact: The SCL0 line cannot be driven low within I2C timing limits, and the bus would be heavily loaded. Communication on the J5 I2C header would fail or be unreliable.

anomalies.observed: The TPS61040 boost feedback divider uses R17 = 1.8M (top, FB to +12V) and R16 = 205k (bottom, FB to GND). With the 0.2 V feedback reference, this sets the output to about 0.2 × (1 + 1.8M/205k) ≈ 2 V, not the +12V rail the net name and the boost stage imply.
anomalies.expected: A 12 V output from a 0.2 V feedback reference needs a bottom resistor of about 30 kΩ for a 1.8 MΩ top resistor (ratio ≈ 59).
anomalies.impact: The +12V boost rail would regulate near 2 V instead of 12 V, which would starve or fail any 12 V load on that rail.

anomalies.observed: In the LTC4412 ideal-diode stage, the PMOS Q1 has its source (Q1.2) on +5V, which is the LTC4412 SENSE node (U6.6), and its drain (Q1.3) on USBC_VBUS_IN, which is the LTC4412 VIN node (U6.1). The device's input-side source arrangement appears reversed relative to a standard VIN-to-load ideal diode.
anomalies.expected: For reverse-current blocking, the PMOS source should sit on the VIN (USB VBUS) side and its drain on the load side (+5V), so the body diode is oriented to block reverse flow.
